statement.p: Find the mass of the solid bounded by the xy-plane, yz-plane, xz-plane, and the plane (x/2)+(y/4)+(z/8) = 1, if the density of the solid is given by \delta (x,y,z)=x + 4 y.

static.solution:
z = 8 - 4 x - 2 y. Note that the projection of this into the xy-plane is the triangular region below y = 4 - 2 x.
The mass of the volume is then M = \int_R \delta\,dV = \int_0^2\int_0^{4 - 2 x}\int_0^{8-4 x-2 y}\,x + 4 y\,dz\,dy\,dx. Integrating with respect to z, M = \int_0^2\int_0^{4 - 2 x} (x + 4 y)(8-4 x-2 y)\,dy\,dx so that M = \int_0^2\int_0^{4 - 2 x} -4 x^2 + 8 x - 2 x y - 16 x y + 32 y - 8 y^2\,dy\,dx. Then, integrating with respect to y, M = \int_0^2 (-4 x^2 + 8 x)(4 - 2 x) + \frac12(32 - 18 x)(4 - 2 x)^2 - \frac{8}{3} (4 - 2 x)^3\,dx. Expanding the these terms, we have M = \int_0^2 \frac{-20}{3} x^3 + 48 x^2 - 112 x + \frac{256}{3}\, dx = 48.
